newsitem.title: THAILAND: Laos rice devastated by rains, help said needed.
newsitem.headline: Laos rice devastated by rains, help said needed.

text.p: Rice crops in key southern growing areas in poverty-stricken Laos have been devastated by severe floods, and emergency food assistance could be required soon, a United Nations relief agency said on Monday.

"The rains have washed away rice crops in major growing provinces and the situation is getting serious," Stephen Keller, emergency coordinator of the U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) in Vientiane, told Reuters by telephone.
"We have asked the Laos government to seek an evaluation by the Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) and the WFP so emergency assistance that is almost certainly needed can be arranged," he added.
Worst hit rice areas so far were the southern and central provinces of Champasak and Souvanakhet, which had lost up to 30 percent or a total of 40,000 hectares of crops, he said.
Widespread flooding and landslides in other growing areas could wreak havoc on the crops there. An assessment was being done, he added.

The worst floods in 30 years in 1995 wiped out crops in land-locked Laos, where rice is the staple, forcing about 23,000 tonnes of emergency rice supplies to be flown to Laos by international relief agencies.
The latest rice harvest was due in November.
"The situation looked worse than in last year as we flew over affected areas last week," Keller said.
He estimated about 30 people may have been killed by severe flooding so far in the country, mostly farmers attempting to save their rice stocks.
